practiceNotes: This is a proposed learning graph, not evidence that any learner has satisfied its prerequisites or performance assessments.

Use spaced repetition for concepts, representations, assumptions, diagnostic distinctions and method selection. Require separate graded proofs, code, laboratory notebooks, analyses and projects for the performance outcomes.

Laboratory activities require appropriate facilities, supervision, training and local risk assessment. Substitute validated datasets or instrument emulators when facilities are unavailable; distinguish those assessments from physical instrument competence.
Biological work requires applicable biosafety, animal-welfare and human-participant approvals. Use nonpathogenic teaching organisms and nonclinical samples unless separately authorized.
Chemical, electrical, laser and ionizing-radiation work requires appropriate controls and authorization. Radiation investigations may use archived spectra rather than radioactive sources.
Security exercises must use owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Human-computer interaction studies require informed consent, accessible participation and proportionate data protection.

Provided computational tools must expose the representations and operations named in each contract. Tool-assisted execution does not establish algorithm implementation or proof competence unless explicitly assessed.
Research-specialization projects use bounded questions and reproducible evidence; they do not imply exhaustive frontier coverage or professional certification.
